original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Prove that the seven-call profile (a,b,p,q,r,s,t)=(2,0,1,1,1,1,1) admits no word in the PR2085/2112 model, because every rational rank-one solution of R+S+T=A+3B=diag(1,3) has an AB or PQ character detecting two calls and four targets.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a larger or nonabelian native alphabet. This package stays in the abelian symmetric 2-by-2 model and answers the named three-frame census profile (2,0,1,1)/(1,1,1) left open by the (0,2,1,1) character exclusion.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the signed-frame escape. This profile still needs eight paid calls, so there is no local call-count saving and no selected-frontier change.
stop_rule: Stop after the character proof for the single named profile (2,0,1,1)/(1,1,1). Do not search the other eighteen census profiles, do not redo (0,2,1,1) or (1,1,1,1), and do not take four-or-more frames.
evidence: Scoped proof that every rational rank-one solution of R+S+T=A+3B has parity image avoiding (1,1), so an AB or PQ form extends and detects two calls against four targets. The scale bracket, Cramer determinant, and axis rearrangement are expanded polynomial identities for bilinear form 3*x1*y1+x2*y2. Lemma 4 is the exhaustive 32-class mod-8 check. The boxes and five fixtures in verify.py corroborate the written argument and are not a solution census.

open_questions.question: Which of the other eighteen three-frame count profiles from the seven-call census survive the same AB/PQ test?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only (1,1,1,1)/(1,1,1), (0,2,1,1)/(1,1,1), and now (2,0,1,1)/(1,1,1) are character-excluded. A surviving profile would be the next place a seven-call three-frame word could exist.
open_questions.first_step: Read one tuple that discussion comment 19377345 already prints, other than (1,1,1,1), (0,2,1,1), and (2,0,1,1). Write that tuple's own residual 4I-aA-bB-pP-qQ and test one rational rank-one solution with the bilinear form of that residual.
open_questions.blocked_by: The forms 3*x1*y1+x2*y2 and x1*y1+3*x2*y2 are special to diag(1,3) and diag(3,1). This package does not name or compute another residual.
